raw_segments.text: The English were preceded in the whale fishery by the Hollanders, Zealanders, and Danes, from
whom they derived many terms still extant in the fishery, and what is yet more, their
fat old fashions, touching plenty to eat and drink, for, as a general thing, the English
merchant ship scrimps her crew, but not so the English whaler.
Hence, in the English, this thing of whaling good cheer is not normal and natural, but
incidental in particular, and therefore must have some special origin, which is here pointed
out and will be still further elucidated.
